passage:
When I moved from Shillong to Bengaluru for college, everything was new at once: the language on the buses, the food, the noise, the fact that nobody noticed if I slept till noon. By October I was eating biscuits for dinner at midnight and crying on the phone to Mom.
So I built a few anchors. One wake time, seven, even on Sundays. A walk round the lake near the hostel every morning before class. Meals in the mess at the same times, even on busy days. And the Thursday choir, where Yusuf, a second-year, saved me a seat in the first week.
None of it was exciting. But when an exam went badly or I missed home, the anchors held. I'm Ira, and I still walk that lake.

qa.q: What does Ira join on Thursdays?
How did Ira feel by October?
qa.a: Ira felt lonely and unsettled, eating biscuits at midnight and crying on the phone to Mom.

qa.q: Which anchors did Ira build, and how did they help?
qa.a: A set wake time, a morning lake walk, regular mess meals and the choir, which held Ira steady when an exam went badly or home felt far away.

qa.q: How might Yusuf have seen the new first-year?
qa.a: Yusuf seemed to see someone new who could use a welcome, and so saved a seat in the very first week.

grounding: A young adult living away from home steadies mood with anchors: a set wake time, a morning walk, regular meals and one fixed social activity.

passage:
Mentor's log, first-year hostel, Pune. Santosh Hegde.
Chinmay has missed three morning labs this fortnight. His roommate says he sleeps at four, skips the mess and plays games online till dawn. When I met him today he looked grey and admitted, "Half the time I don't know what day it is. At home Aai did everything."
We made a small plan together, with Chinmay choosing each part: an alarm at seven every day, breakfast in the mess before lab, a walk to the gate and back, and one fixed thing each week to look forward to. He picked the Saturday football match.
I'll check in next week. He shook my hand as he left, a little embarrassed but lighter.

qa.q: How many morning labs had Chinmay missed?
qa.a: Chinmay missed three morning labs this fortnight.

qa.q: How did Chinmay feel admitting he didn't know what day it was?
qa.a: Chinmay felt lost and a little embarrassed, missing the structure Aai used to give.

qa.q: Why was it wise to let Chinmay choose each part of the plan?
qa.a: Anchors Chinmay picks himself, like the seven o'clock alarm and Saturday football, are more likely to stick than rules handed down.

qa.q: How might Chinmay's roommate have been affected by the late nights?
qa.a: The roommate may have been disturbed by the gaming till dawn and worried enough to mention it.

grounding: A young adult away from home is steadied by anchors: a set wake time, regular meals, a short walk and one fixed social activity.
